propositions: Requiring literal section headings (Approach, Scope) as oracle for plan validity is unsound; semantic aliases and compact executable plans without headings pass both plan-review and completion-verifier attestations.
Deterministic placeholder/phrase lexicon matchers (e.g., 'check if') produce false positives on mechanically decidable conditional work; the same tickets with such phrases are signed and completed.
Explicit per-AC proof-coverage markers ('verified by') are not required for valid plans; behavioral assertions and oracles are precise even without sentinel markers and pass both attestations.
Empty file_impact is valid for analysis, probe, and read-only operational tickets with explicit no-edit/output contracts; requiring edit-set on such work invents nonexistent repository changes.
Conjunction/vagueness counts on AC text cannot reliably distinguish atomic bundled deliverables from split independent work; deterministic counting is unsuitable as hard failure criteria.
Testing section headings do not obligate negative scenario coverage; applicability is semantic (new user-facing behavior) not triggered by heading presence alone.
